newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: S.Africa Feb gold/forex reserves over 12 bln rand.
newsitem.headline: S.Africa Feb gold/forex reserves over 12 bln rand.

text.p: The South African Reserve Bank said on Tuesday provisional gross gold and foreign exchange reserves amounted to 12.5 billion rand as at February 28, 1997 compared to 11.8 billion rand as at January 31.

The bank said in a statement it utilised foreign credit lines to the value of 2.1 billion rand during February in part to fund the redemption of South Africa's ECU 250 million rand bond issue which fell due for repayment on February 10. Funds were also used to augment the bank's foreign exchange liquidity.
According to a Reuters consensus poll of 10 economists, gross reserves were expected to climb to 12.4 billion rand in February -- the highest level since March 1996.

Reserve figures were only expected to be released on Friday but the bank said owing to the importance attached to these monthly figures it had been decided to release them as soon as possible after month-end.
A bank official told Reuters the decision had been taken late on Tuesday afternoon by bank governor Chris Stals.

"Dr Stals decided late this afternoon that he wanted the figures in the market as soon as possible. It looks like (the release) will happen like this frequently and it may even be by the second working date of every month," the official said.
The official said the release of the data was previously only done once the bank's monthly statement of assets and liabilities had been finalised.

The statement from the bank said that the reserve figures released on Tuesday were only preliminary and any possible changes would be reflected in the monthly statement which would be published on Friday.
